facts.text: Rogers was founded in 1897 and named after railroad engineer John Rogers, whose work helped bring the Great Northern Railway through the area.
Norwegian and German immigrants settled Rogers, focusing on agriculture and building homes, stores, and community buildings amid harsh winters and land clearing.
Rogers sits in the Drift Prairie, a landscape of glacial till and outwash, and lies near the Sheyenne River valley that shapes local farmland.
The town’s short growing season of about 144 days forces farmers to use frost‑protective techniques to keep crops alive.
Rogers survived the 1910–1911 floods and hosted annual threshing bees from the 1920s through the 1940s, a testament to its resilient farming community.
